notes: monthsInDate is load-bearing and is NOT a case form. Maltese does not decline its months; it inserts the preposition ta' between the day and the month, so the first of January is 1 ta' Jannar and never 1 Jannar. Carrying the ta' inside monthsInDate lets LL stay the plain D MMMM YYYY without the formatter needing an escaped literal. The WEEKDAY NAMES CARRY THE DEFINITE ARTICLE as part of the name — Il-Ħadd, It-Tnejn, L-Erbgħa — and the article assimilates to the following consonant, which is why the seven do not share one prefix; the short forms drop it. Weekdays are listed Sunday-first because the formatter wants them so, while date/weekday.txt in the pack is Monday-first as a Maltese calendar prints it. Malta writes dates DD/MM/YYYY with slashes, the British way, and uses the 24-hour clock in writing with a colon (14:30). The decimal separator is a full stop and the thousands separator a comma (1,234.56), again British rather than continental, which is a trap for a euro-area locale. Month and weekday names are CAPITALISED. Ġun and Diċ carry dotted letters: strip the diacritics and the abbreviation stops being Maltese.
